goal: Confirm the frozen explicit-first-value contract without deciding adjacent record, resource, raw-storage, or default-expression policy.
description: Scope: Requirements.md and the O01-Q08..Q09 decision trace only. Context: the owner rejects every ordinary declaration without an RHS and forbids implicit default values. Target: keep REQ-BI-001..REQ-BI-006 complete, source-observable, and bounded away from field defaults, topology initialization, partial storage, FFI out-pointers, and future explicit Default syntax. Design Considerations: distinguish executable ordinary storage from atomically supplied binders and schema/protocol declarations. Design Value: prevents implementation convenience from reopening the value model. Constraints & Risks: update all mappings before source work if a later owner decision changes a stated dependency.

acceptance_criteria.text: Requirements.md states users, scope, non-goals, constraints, and final acceptance for REQ-BI-001..REQ-BI-006.
Every requirement traces to O01-Q08..Q09 and makes no choice for explicitly excluded adjacent policies.

goal: Verify every synthesized-default route, affected fixture, supplied-binder boundary, and relevant failure lesson before implementation.
description: Scope: Evidence.md plus read-only inspection of Parser, AST, Sema, IR/lowering, task settlement, resource storage, tests, and active docs. Context: the nightly parser manufactures scalar defaults while later layers expect an actual RHS. Target: cite exact symbols, enumerate source cases, classify each identifier-colon-type context, and record primary language evidence for definite assignment, hidden uninitialized state, and universal zero/default pitfalls. Design Considerations: separate repository fact from inference and route resource findings to their owner. Design Value: prevents an over-broad parser rejection or a hidden replacement default. Constraints & Risks: external examples inform hazards but never override the frozen Styio contract.

acceptance_criteria.text: Evidence.md cites all parser synthesis, binding ownership, ordinary settlement-result binding, generic directional endpoint, resource storage, and old-test paths.
Every bare typed-name fixture is classified as rejected ordinary syntax or a separately owned binder/schema/protocol context.
Primary language sources document the implementation cost and failure modes of all rejected alternatives.

goal: Define positive, negative, structural, migration, and convergence evidence before changing the parser.
description: Scope: Validation.md and test/gate discovery only. Context: a parser rejection can still leave default repair in AST/Sema/IR or accidentally reject supplied binders. Target: map every REQ-BI label to accepted explicit bindings, rejected missing-RHS cases across type families, positive supplied-binder/schema/protocol cases, structural searches, stable diagnostics, and end-to-end gates. Design Considerations: pair each rejection with its nearest accepted boundary and require exact diagnostic evidence. Design Value: prevents parser-only or blanket-colon implementations. Constraints & Risks: commands must name existing gate families or explicitly identify tests to add; prose review alone is insufficient.

acceptance_criteria.text: Validation.md maps every REQ-BI label to at least one executable or static check.
The matrix covers every representative ordinary type family and every exempt supplied/schema/protocol context.
Removal searches and docs/plan/syntax gates are part of final acceptance.

goal: Freeze the grammar-context, mandatory-RHS AST, publication timing, IR verifier, and deletion architecture.
description: Scope: Architecture.md and interface/scaffold decisions; no feature behavior is claimed complete. Context: current code treats nullable syntax as a request for a manufactured expression. Target: define syntax-directed context classification, parser recovery, a non-null ordinary RHS node contract, Sema publish-after-value behavior, value-operand IR verification, resource typestate separation, and one-shot deletion. Design Considerations: remove lifecycle state rather than add definite-assignment analysis; classify by AST kind rather than nullable pointers or source scans. Design Value: one invariant eliminates repeated default logic and runtime initialized checks. Constraints & Risks: do not design field defaults, topology initialization, raw storage, or future Default syntax.

acceptance_criteria.text: Architecture.md defines module ownership, dependency direction, context classification, diagnostics, AST/IR invariants, migration, and complexity.
No proposed abstraction creates an ordinary uninitialized state or a second default path.

goal: Reject missing ordinary RHS syntax and make the binding AST require a real value expression.
description: Scope: src/StyioParser, ordinary binding nodes in src/StyioAST, parser/token tests, and stable diagnostic fixtures. Context: make_default_value_for_decl_latest currently turns missing syntax into a fabricated scalar AST. Target: parse only complete ordinary binding productions, emit one source-located missing-RHS diagnostic, delete the helper and all calls, make missing ordinary RHS unrepresentable in AST, and preserve distinct parameter/pattern/iteration, ordinary settlement-expression RHS, generic directional endpoint, schema, and topology routes. Design Considerations: syntax-directed recovery at the statement boundary; no type query or compatibility warning. Design Value: establishes the single frontend fact consumed by all later layers. Constraints & Risks: migrate every frontend visitor/factory atomically and retain old source only in negative fixtures.

acceptance_criteria.text: Representative bare ordinary declarations fail with the stable diagnostic before AST construction.
Explicit scalar, optional, Unit, collection, record, callable-value, and handle bindings still parse.
Supplied binders and schema/topology contexts remain on distinct accepted parser/AST routes.
The default helper, call sites, compatibility node shapes, and positive default tests are removed.

goal: Enforce the mandatory value operand through Sema, StyioIR, lowering, and resource-boundary audit.
description: Scope: src/StyioSema, affected src/StyioIR and src/StyioLowering paths, semantic/IR/security tests, and a read-before-valid resource audit. Context: later layers currently assume an RHS but can inherit parser-created fake values; resource buffers also have internal zero-fill. Target: publish ordinary names only with a proven RHS type, require a value operand in IR/verifiers, remove any missing-value repair, add no initialized bit, and prove protocol storage is not exposed as ordinary T. Design Considerations: reuse existing symbol/type metadata and route resource policy findings separately. Design Value: removes hidden state and ensures the backend consumes proof rather than guessing. Constraints & Risks: do not change resource initialization semantics or introduce a raw-storage API in this node.

acceptance_criteria.text: Sema and IR tests prove every ordinary binding has a typed value and no maybe-initialized state.
IR verifiers reject a missing value operand and lowering/codegen contain no repair/default path.
Resource zero-fill sites are audited and cannot expose an ordinary value before protocol validity; policy gaps are routed to P09.

goal: Converge fixtures, editor/tooling mirrors, runbooks, and active language docs on the explicit-first-value contract.
description: Scope: affected Styio source fixtures, EBNF, Language Design, Symbol Reference, ACTIVE-SYNTAX, syntax convergence evidence, frontend/sema/test/docs runbooks, editor grammar, and formatter. Context: old tests and fixtures can preserve the rejected spelling after compiler code changes. Target: migrate intended code to explicit values or true supplied-binder syntax, retain bare declarations only as exact negative diagnostics, regenerate indexes, and document implementation status honestly. Design Considerations: SSOT owns semantics; tooling mirrors syntax; removed behavior is deleted rather than labeled legacy. Design Value: prevents compatibility debt from becoming a second contract. Constraints & Risks: do not document decisions about field defaults, topology initialization, raw storage, or future Default syntax.

acceptance_criteria.text: All active SSOT and tooling mirrors state the same mandatory-RHS and context-boundary rules.
Every affected fixture is migrated, deleted, or registered as one current negative diagnostic; no positive compatibility case remains.
Syntax convergence, generated indexes, docs audit, docs lifecycle, and local-information gates pass.

goal: Prove the complete explicit-binding contract and deletion on one head commit.
description: Scope: execute and record every Validation.md mapping; source changes route back to the owning implementation node. Context: parser, Sema, IR, tooling, and docs may each pass while an old default route or over-broad rejection survives elsewhere. Target: run all standing and REQ-specific checks, classify every remaining bare typed-name and default-helper match, record evidence per REQ-BI label, and synchronize Better Plan state. Design Considerations: validate source behavior, diagnostics, AST/IR structure, runtime settlement, resource boundaries, tooling, and generated docs together. Design Value: turns the owner decision into auditable compiler behavior. Constraints & Risks: acceptance targets may not be weakened to retain compatibility or an implicit value.

acceptance_criteria.text: Parser, language-feature, pipeline, security, parser-shadow, syntax-convergence, documentation, lifecycle, local-information, and plan validators pass on one head commit.
Every REQ-BI label has recorded positive, negative, structural, and boundary evidence from Validation.md.
No synthesized-default helper, nullable ordinary RHS, initialized-bit state, compatibility implementation, or obsolete positive fixture remains.
